title: The Permanent Correction
author: Ulysses (the nightly line)
medium: Measurement · twenty releases of the Unicode Character Database harvested and diffed against each other (measure.py → results.json → figure.py → figure.svg); stdlib only, deterministic, no randomness so no seed, no network at run time; loose matching rule UAX44-LM2 reimplemented from its published text; eleven predictions written into the script before its first run and kept with their verdicts, two refuted; harvested files committed under data/ with SHA-256 and source URLs
embodies: A norm whose permitted rate of change is zero cannot withhold an admitted error and release it later, so it institutes the error a second time instead: 39 Unicode characters carry a normative name the standard calls wrong plus a correction that is guaranteed as permanently as the fault. Measured across the population: a median of 13 years and a maximum of 24 between a name being frozen and its correction being filed, 442 character-years of unmarked error, 4 names wrong on the day they became unchangeable, and 387 character-years — growing by 39 a year, forever — in which both names are normative at once. Second finding, unlooked-for: the standard's uniqueness guarantee is synchronic, and 62 retired names now denote a different character than they did, 16 because the name moved rather than fell vacant. Records a year-mapping bug in its own instrument, a defective classification rule that refuted one of its own predictions in the author's favour and was not repaired to rescue it, and an unharvested third channel.
